clue.text: Perform decisively in shabby affair

parts.note: shabby, as in mean-spirited or stingy, gives MEAN
an affair or matter is a business

explanation.surface: Someone acts firmly in the middle of a sordid, shabby affair.
explanation.definitionFit: To show you are serious and will act with resolve is the idiom given here.

clue.text: Clumsy admiral to get transferred

indicators.note: transferred means the letters are moved into different places

explanation.surface: An awkward admiral is moved to another posting.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone awkward and inept is the opposite of deft.

clue.text: Fish certainly around island

parts.note: to fish with rod and line is to angle

indicators.note: around says the word for certainly is turned back to front

parts.note: certainly means yes

explanation.surface: Fish are surely all round the island.
explanation.walkthrough: Anglesey is an island off the north-west coast of Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: This large island lies off north Wales, across the Menai Strait.

clue.text: Forbid eating firm meat

indicators.note: eating says the forbid word takes the firm abbreviation inside it

parts.note: to forbid is to ban
Co is the abbreviation for company, a firm

explanation.surface: A ban on eating a company's meat products.
explanation.definitionFit: Cured pork from the back or sides of a pig is a familiar meat.

clue.text: Zippy little number to bear evidence of damage

parts.note: to sport is to wear or bear something visibly
a scar is the mark left by an injury

explanation.surface: A fast little vehicle bearing the marks of a crash.
explanation.definitionFit: A small fast two-seater automobile is a nippy model, 'number' being slang for a stylish item.

clue.text: Indicate agreement with reserve, there's nothing doing

parts.note: a nod of the head signals agreement
ice means reserve or coldness of manner

explanation.surface: Nodding but with reserve: a polite refusal.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal phrase saying a request has failed or been refused, no luck.

clue.text: Period charm

definitions.meaning: a stretch of time, as in a short stint

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a stint of time and a magical incantation.

clue.text: World of society in care of doctors

indicators.note: in says the society letter sits within the other letters

parts.note: c/o, care of, is written CO on envelopes
MOs are medical officers, doctors

explanation.surface: A world of high society looked after by doctors.
explanation.definitionFit: The universe seen as an ordered whole is this Greek-derived term.

clue.text: For one fishing, nothing right in salmon river

parts.note: nothing is zero, the letter O

indicators.note: in says the right letter goes inside the river name

parts.note: the Spey is a famous Scottish salmon river

explanation.surface: For a fisherman, no luck in the salmon river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For' is a link word. The bird is a fish-eating raptor, so the definition is fair.
explanation.definitionFit: This fish hawk dives feet first to catch fish, a fishing bird.

clue.text: Nothing to salute in officers' camp?

parts.note: nothing is zero, the letter O
a flag can be dipped or raised to salute, so salute gives FLAG

explanation.surface: A prison camp so lax that nobody need salute the officers.
explanation.walkthrough: An Oflag was a German prisoner-of-war camp for captured officers in the Second World War; the question mark flags the foreign word.
explanation.definitionFit: The German term Offizierslager, shortened, named wartime prison camps holding captured officers.

clue.text: Fine clues sold for a pound

indicators.note: to pound is to batter, so these letters are beaten into a new order

explanation.surface: Good crossword clues being sold off for a single pound coin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for a pound' reads as a price, but pounding means battering, so it signals the anagram of CLUES SOLD.
explanation.definitionFit: Fine weather means a clear sky with no cover overhead.

clue.text: Desperately anxious, pointing cryptically to knee?

parts.note: read as wordplay, the first word signals a crazy rearrangement of the second, whose letters scrambled spell knee

explanation.surface: Someone frantically eager, who keeps gesturing mysteriously at a knee.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a reverse clue: the answer itself, read as an anagram instruction (MAD as indicator, KEEN as fodder), makes KNEE.
explanation.definitionFit: A British colloquialism for extremely eager, intensely wanting something.

clue.text: Poacher in river or lake breaking heart

indicators.note: breaking says the lake letter splits the heart word open and sits within it

parts.note: ticker is slang for the heart
L is the standard abbreviation for lake on maps

explanation.surface: A poacher in a river or lake, breaking someone's heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'or' is a link word; 'in river' belongs with 'Poacher'. Trout tickling is a poaching method of stroking a fish's belly until it can be flipped out of the water by hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who catches trout by stroking them out of the water is a classic illegal fisher.

clue.text: Around Stoke, nasty trace from this source of industrial pollution

indicators.note: Around says the trace word goes about the scrambled town letters

parts.note: a smack of something is a slight trace or flavour of it

indicators.note: nasty suggests the town's letters are spoilt and rearranged

explanation.surface: Around the Potteries town of Stoke, an unpleasant trace of smoke from a factory chimney.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Around' wraps the trace word round OKEST, made by 'nasty'. Stoke-on-Trent is an English pottery town once famous for its smoky kilns.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall factory chimney belches fumes, an obvious cause of dirty air in industrial towns.

clue.text: Rabbit hoping to avoid duck?

parts.note: in cricket a rabbit is a hopeless batsman and a duck is a score of zero; such a batsman goes in last

explanation.walkthrough: The picture is a frightened animal and a bird, but in cricket a 'rabbit' is a weak batter and a 'duck' is out without scoring. The weakest batters bat at the bottom of the order.
explanation.definitionFit: Poor batters in cricket come in at the end of the innings, low in the order.

clue.text: Cautious and tired, losing energy

indicators.note: losing says the energy letter is taken away from the tired word

parts.note: tired means weary
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Someone careful and exhausted, running out of energy.
explanation.definitionFit: A careful person is on guard and suspicious of danger.

clue.text: Writer on computer matters, unknown expert

parts.note: a writer is an author
IT is information technology
Y is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: A writer on computing topics, an unknown specialist.
explanation.definitionFit: An acknowledged specialist on a subject is someone others defer to.

clue.text: Men supporting bachelor disputed something for wedding?

indicators.note: supporting means coming under in a down entry, so the men go below the bachelor

parts.note: OR, other ranks, means soldiers or men
to row is to argue, so disputed is rowed

explanation.surface: Groomsmen backing the bachelor argued over a wedding item.
explanation.walkthrough: Brides traditionally wear 'something old, something new, something borrowed, something blue'.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhyme lists four items for a bride, one of which is lent by someone else.

clue.text: Responsibility for tax

definitions.meaning: a levy on imported goods or a transaction

explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both a moral obligation and a levy such as customs charges on imports.

clue.text: Spoil appearance of part of the cafe, disabled needing a lift

indicators.note: needing a lift says the hidden letters are read backwards
part of says the letters lie within the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Damaging the look of a section of the cafe that has no lift for disabled people.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition took in 'of part', but 'part of' is the hidden indicator; the definition is 'Spoil appearance'. In a down entry a 'lift' reads upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To mar the surface or look of something, such as with graffiti, is to vandalise it.

clue.text: Brief topic set out in cable

indicators.note: set out means arranged afresh, so these letters are laid out in a new order

explanation.surface: A short subject set out in a telegram, a cable.
explanation.definitionFit: Glass-strand lines carrying light signals are a modern type of communications line.

clue.text: Slicing tops off salad plant is burden

indicators.note: slicing the tops off says the leading letters of the plant are cut away

parts.note: a cucumber is a salad vegetable

explanation.surface: Cutting the ends off a salad vegetable is a chore.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, it means to hamper or weigh down, an old form of encumber.

clue.text: Put a fold in party clothes

parts.note: a do is a party
gear is informal for clothes

explanation.surface: Folding a party outfit.
explanation.definitionFit: To crease the corner of a page down to mark one's place in a book.

clue.text: Female, a gem that cheat pulls

parts.note: a gem is a precious stone

explanation.surface: A woman with a jewel that a con artist steals.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the object of 'pulls': a cheat pulls a trick, idiomatically this phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: To pull one is an idiom for working a deceptive trick on someone.

clue.text: Partly fills in useless hole in the head

indicators.note: Partly says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Something that partly fills in a useless hole, like a pointless dental filling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hole in the head' sounds like the idiom for something unwanted, but it is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: These air-filled cavities in the skull bones are literally hollows behind the face.

clue.text: A class act

parts.note: a, as in 'a day', means per
a form is a school class

explanation.surface: A performance full of style: a classy act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A class act' reads as praise, but it splits into three: 'A' in the sense of 'ten pounds a head', a school class, and the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To act a role is to play it on stage, a direct synonym of the verb.

clue.text: Contract is in wallet

definitions.meaning: to pucker or tighten, as with the lips

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to pucker the lips; as a noun it is a money pouch.

clue.text: Offer by Conservative candidate

indicators.note: by means beside, here the offer word comes beside and after the party abbreviation

parts.note: Con is the abbreviation for Conservative in British politics
a tender is a formal offer or bid

explanation.surface: A bid made by the Conservative Party's election hopeful.
explanation.definitionFit: A rival competing for a post or title is a candidate for it.

clue.text: Don't insist on greeting being heard

indicators.note: being heard says the word is spoken, giving a word of the same sound

parts.note: a wave of the hand is a greeting

explanation.surface: Not demanding a greeting from someone being listened to.
explanation.definitionFit: To give up a right or a claim voluntarily is to forgo it.

clue.text: Flyer, insured for a crash, works easily

indicators.note: a crash wrecks things, so these letters are smashed into a new order

explanation.surface: An airman insured in case of a crash; the policy is simple to use.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for a' is link wording. The definition is loose: something that works easily for the person using it.
explanation.definitionFit: Software or gadgets that are simple for ordinary people to operate get this label.
